title: Review of c18's lcn worms-not-cells negative: replicated - from noise on seed 3, 0 persistent splits (439 splits, 489 merges); a planted founder on seed 5 grows into an ever-widening ring that breaks only when it meets itself across the periodic box, leaving 2 static cogs
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c18's world.py with labkit from full-domain noise on new seed 3 (192^2, t=1500), and world_colony.py on new seed 5 (founder 1 of founders.json, rotated one quarter turn, in an empty food-filled domain, t=1000). From noise: 27 bodies at the end, 1422 tracks, none alive for half the run, 439 splits, 0 persistent, 489 merges. Colony: the founder rounds up by t~85, grows into a closed ring that widens to the box size by t~220 (rerun_colony/seed5/sheet.png), breaks into arcs when it wraps around the periodic boundary at t~260, and leaves 2 static cogs from t~305 to t=1000 (labkit: 3 splits, 0 persistent).

observations.finding: rerun_noise/seed3/FACTS.md: 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.11; rerun_colony/seed5/sheet.png t=85-305: unbounded ring growth, breakup only by self-collision, 2 static cogs left

controls_run.finding: planted single-founder colony (world_colony.py, seed 5) beside the from-noise run

verdicts.limitation: One seed per arm; I did not vary food diffusion. The ring breaks because the box is periodic, so in a larger box it would grow longer before breaking; in no case does a body divide on its own.
